subject.title: WhatsApp 1:1: inbound image wedges main lane ~3min before processing — multimodal run strands active_reply_work/queued_work_without_active_run (repro on 2026.6.10, post-#95039)

question: Should OpenClaw treat run:completed plus queued_work_without_active_run as authoritative enough to clear active_reply_work for WhatsApp multimodal direct turns, or keep the current active-work protection until stronger live proof lands?
rationale: The source path and logs show a real stall signature, but the fix changes when recovery may release work that still looks active, so automation should not pick the session-state policy alone.

options.title: Sponsor focused recovery fix
options.body: Accept the reporter's terminal-progress evidence, require live WhatsApp proof, and implement a bounded clear/release path for stale active_reply_work after completed multimodal runs.

options.title: Fold into broader WhatsApp tracker
options.body: Route this issue under the open WhatsApp replay/lane tracker if maintainers decide the image loop has the same remaining root cause as that broader work.

options.title: Wait for current-main repro
options.body: Keep the issue open under needs-live-repro and avoid recovery-policy changes until someone captures the loop on current main.

recommendation.title: Sponsor focused recovery fix
recommendation.body: Accept the reporter's terminal-progress evidence, require live WhatsApp proof, and implement a bounded clear/release path for stale active_reply_work after completed multimodal runs.

likelyOwner.reason: openperf authored the closest merged stuck-session recovery fix and is the strongest history signal for this recovery-policy choice.
